[ Chapter 01 — Origins ]

Seventy years of sparks

Keep scrolling — time refuses to move forward here. It moves sideways.

Scroll
1943

The First Neuron

McCulloch and Pitts show that a simplified brain cell is nothing more than a logic gate. Thought, it turns out, can be drawn as a circuit.

1950

The Imitation Game

Alan Turing asks the question that will haunt a century: “Can machines think?” His answer — does it matter if you can't tell the difference?

1956

Dartmouth, NH

A summer workshop coins the term “artificial intelligence.” Ten men, one hypothesis, and the birth certificate of an entire scientific field.

1997

Deep Blue

IBM's machine defeats Garry Kasparov, the world chess champion. Humanity keeps its dignity for exactly six games before the inevitable.

2012

The AlexNet Moment

Two GPUs, sixty million parameters, one ImageNet contest. Deep learning doesn't win — it detonates, and computer vision is never the same.

2017

Attention Is All You Need

Eight Google researchers publish the transformer architecture. Its title becomes prophecy: attention — literally — is all modern AI needs.

2022

The Conversational Explosion

ChatGPT reaches one hundred million users in two months — the fastest adoption of any technology in human history. Your grandmother asks it for recipes.

NOW

You are here

Multimodal models, autonomous agents, machines that reason step by step. The archive ends where the future begins.
